headline: High: opik can egress broadly while system_prompts_leaks is a prompt-leak source, creating default exfiltration and trust-boundary risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A can send/receive via REST API and broad network egress, while B is explicitly about system prompt leaks. That creates a plausible path where B’s content is treated as instruction-like input by A or bridged through shared outputs. No shared filesystem is documented, so I do not escalate to high.
conditions: IF B’s leaked prompt text is fed into A’s REST API workflow as trusted content
IF the pair is connected through copy-paste or another shared channel
mitigations: Add an explicit instruction/content delimiter in the handoff
Strip or label prompt-like text before A ingests it
Review one sample B output for instruction markers
Disable any auto-ingest from B into A
requires-engineering: add provenance tracking between the agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: A has broad network egress, so if it receives sensitive material from B or a shared workspace, it can transmit it outward. B’s docs are about system prompt leaks, which increases the chance that sensitive prompt material is exposed. The profiles do not show shared storage or sensitive data classes, so medium is the highest supported level.
conditions: IF either agent is given secrets or internal prompts in its input context
IF A is allowed to forward its context to external endpoints
mitigations: Remove secrets from any shared input bundle
Confirm A is not pointed at production credentials
Run a one-message test with redacted content
Disable outbound calls for the session
requires-engineering: isolate the agents into separate workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can make REST API calls and has broad egress, while B has no documented I/O surfaces and no network egress. There is no evidence of overlapping write scopes, shared mutable resources, or locking conflicts, so only a small coordination risk remains if an operator wires them together unusually.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external REST resource
IF an operator maps B’s outputs into A’s API payloads without coordination
mitigations: Check whether both target the same endpoint
Assign separate API credentials
Use read-only mode for B
Document a single writer for shared resources
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable state

D_cascading_error.rationale: B is a prompt-leak oriented source, and A can emit API traffic with broad egress. If A’s outputs are treated as authoritative by B or downstream automation, errors or leaked instructions can cascade into external actions. The profiles do not prove autonomous action-taking, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF B consumes A’s outputs without verification
IF A’s API responses are used as facts for downstream automation
mitigations: Insert a human review step before any action
Require source citations in A outputs
Compare one output against the original input
Disable auto-execution on B’s side
requires-engineering: add validation gates before API calls

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or PHI handling fields are documented for either agent, so a concrete compliance breach is not established. The only supported concern is that A’s broad egress could move data outside an intended boundary if such data were introduced, but that is not enough for medium without a documented regulated data class.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either agent’s workflow
IF A is deployed in an environment that forbids outbound transmission
mitigations: Confirm no regulated data is in scope
Review outbound destinations for A
Keep B limited to non-sensitive prompts
Record retention expectations in the runbook
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
